title: Operator trust-tiering and minimal audit pathway (PRD draft)
content:
Context and goal:
This is an early product PRD draft exploring a lightweight alternative to our full attestation/approval pipeline for common operator workflows in customer-managed networking. The idea: introduce a trust-tier model for operators (Admin, Maintainer, ReadOnly, ScopedOperator) and a configurable "mini-audit" pathway that reduces friction for low-risk changes while still producing compact, queryable evidence for post-hoc investigations.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Full approval + evidence capture is robust but expensive in operator time and storage; customers doing frequent predictable ops (e.g., IP range updates, ephemeral peering toggles) push back on heavy handoffs.
- We need a predictable, auditable surface that scales to high-frequency operator actions without losing forensic value when incidents happen.
- Existing PRDs are focused on heavy attestation + immutable ledgers. This document proposes a middle tier: lower friction for low-risk ops + sampled, cryptographically-signed compact proofs for forensic rehydration.

High-level proposal (what we will build):
1) Trust tiers: short classification that maps to policy and evidence requirements.
   - Admin: full approval chain, mandatory evidence bundle, longest retention.
   - ScopedOperator: can perform a bounded set of operations (pre-approved templates) with lightweight on-change receipts.
   - Maintainer: changes require local approval or a one-step consent; evidence is compact and sampled.
   - ReadOnly: no mutation privileges.
2) Mini-audit pathway (for ScopedOperator & Maintainer templates):
   - On operation: produce a compact-proof token (base64 JSON blob) containing: actor id, operation template id, small diff summary, signed timestamp, nonce. Token stored in customer-managed evidence store (S3 or vault hook) and indexed in Redwood compact index.
   - Sampling policy: default 10% full evidence retention, 90% compact tokens. Sampling configurable by customer and by template risk score.
   - Rapid rollback affordance: compact proofs include reversible-change hints to help automated rollback tools reconstruct state with minimal telemetry.
3) Approval gates and UX patterns:
   - In-line quick-approve: for changes under X risk score and when performed by ScopedOperator with active delegation. Quick UI confirmation with short rationale text.
   - Escalation-on-failure: if autoscan detects anomaly post-change, the system auto-grabs full evidence from customer store (if available) and escalates to Admin chain.

API / contract sketch (developer-facing):
- POST /ops/v1/execute-template -> returns { compact_proof_token, op_id, status }
- GET /ops/v1/proof/{op_id} -> returns compact token + pointer to full bundle (if stored)
- Webhook: /webhooks/proof-sampled -> ping SRE/CS when a sampled full-bundle is stored (for compliance customers)
Notes: compact_proof_token is a signed envelope (Ed25519) containing a minimal JSON structure. The signature key metadata must be exportable to customer KMS if they are on Private deployments.

Storage model and privacy considerations:
- Default: compact tokens stored in Redwood compact index (TTL configurable). Full bundles stored optionally in customer-managed object store; Redwood stores only pointers and hash digests when customers choose this path.
- For regulated customers: offer an "escrow-only" mode where full evidence never leaves customer-controlled storage; Redwood can request retrieval under specific audit flows.

Observability & acceptance criteria:
- Metrics: mean time to approve for ScopedOperator flows (target: <30s for quick-approve), percent of ops with compact token only, storage delta vs full-attestation pipeline (expect 60–80% reduction in retention size).
- SLOs: compact-proofs indexed within 5s of operation 95% of the time.
- Security: signature verification must fail-open only to flag; never auto-accept unsigned tokens.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (prototype): implement compact token format + local signer in sandbox; internal-only templates for network-ops team.
- Phase 1 (pilot): enable ScopedOperator templates for 3 customers with frequent low-risk ops; add sampling dashboards.
- Phase 2 (GA): expose UI flows in Console, build customer-managed storage connectors and KMS key import docs.

Operational playbooks and runbooks (sketch):
- Operator incident: if anomaly triggers escalation, SRE runs "evidence-reconstruct" that pulls sampled full bundles (or requests from customer store) and reconstructs diff. Provide a checklist for evidence retrieval and communication with customer.
- Data retention: by default compact tokens retained 90 days; sampled full bundles retention matches customer SLA.

Open questions / tradeoffs (explicit):
- Sampling rates: how aggressive is safe? Need empirical workload study.
- Risk scoring: who defines template risk? Product + solutions engineering to define heuristics; allow customer overrides.
- KMS integration: importing customer keys into Redwood for signing vs letting customers sign tokens themselves — both have UX and trust tradeoffs.
- Legal/compliance: are compact tokens legally sufficient for some audits? Need legal input.

Implementation notes and TODOs (engineering-facing):
- Define compact token schema (fields + max size 1.5KB).
- Build signer interface that supports Redwood-managed keys and customer KMS-backed keys.
- Add indexer pipeline change: compact index + pointer store with HMAC digests.
- Console: quick-approve modal + template editor + trust-tier admin panel.
- E2E test matrix: simulate high-frequency template runs + randomized sampling; measure index latency and storage saved.

Acceptance criteria for GA:
- Pilot customers report >50% reduction in operator friction vs full-attestation path.
- Sampling dashboards show retrieval latency < 10s for sampled full bundles.
- Security review sign-off on signature portability and non-repudiation model.

Appendix: Example compact token (illustrative, shortened):
{
  "actor_id": "svc-netops-42",
  "template_id": "peer-toggle-v1",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-07T17:28:12Z",
  "diff_summary": "peer:us-west-2:abcd -> enabled",
  "nonce": "kZ4f...",
  "sig_meta": "key-id:rdw-sign-v2"
}--signed--

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight: think of this as the "silver" option between full attestation (gold) and no-evidence (bronze).
- Looking for feedback on: default sampling %, trusted key model, and API ergonomics for customers with on-prem object stores.

Quick checklist for next steps before team review: 
- [ ] Run a 2-week simulation on staging with synthetic network ops traffic (Marco)
- [ ] Draft legal note on compact tokens and audit sufficiency (Tina)
- [ ] Security review of signer interface (Leah)
- [ ] UX mockups for quick-approve & trust-tier admin (Samir)

-- end --
